issues.legal_issue: A payment that a tenant has agreed to make to the landlord for use and occupation of the premises, in addition to the stated rent, forms part of rent.
material_facts: The written lease set monthly rent and separately required the tenant to pay the landlord an amount equal to half the annual property tax.
The tenant did not pay the agreed property-tax amounts.
issues.conclusion: The agreed property-tax payment formed part of the rent for the purposes of the eviction claim.
issues.legal_principle: The Act did not define rent, so the Court applied its ordinary meaning. Under Karani Properties Ltd. v. Miss Augustine and the Madras High Court's approach in Messrs. Raval and Company v. K.G. Ramachandran, rent encompasses payments agreed to be made to the landlord for use and occupation of the premises and associated amenities; an agreed payment of property tax to the landlord therefore forms part of rent.

predicates.tenant_rent_control_proceeding: A landlord seeks a tenant's eviction in a proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.tenant_agreed_occupancy_charge: The tenant agreed to pay the landlord a charge, in addition to stated rent, for use and occupation of the premises.

issues.definition: When a tenant agrees in a rent-control eviction proceeding to pay the landlord an additional charge for use and occupation of the premises, that charge is treated as rent.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant's failure to clear rent arrears after a two-month landlord's notice is wilful unless the tenant proves inability to pay due to unavoidable circumstances.
material_facts: The tenant owed monthly rent and agreed property-tax payments, both of which the Court treated as rent.
The landlord served a notice demanding the arrears and waited the required two-month period before starting eviction proceedings.
The tenant tendered only the monthly rent and did not pay the property-tax arrears, so the full amount demanded remained unpaid.
The tenant did not claim that unavoidable circumstances had made the tenant incapable of paying.
issues.conclusion: The tenant committed wilful default and was liable to eviction; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10(2)(i) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, and its Explanation, default continuing after a landlord's two-month notice to clear arrears is wilful. S. Sundaram v. V.R. Pattabhiraman holds that such continued non-payment is conclusive proof of wilfulness unless the tenant proves inability to pay because of unavoidable circumstances.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_proceeding and landlord_gave_two_month_arrears_notice and rent_arrears_remained_after_notice and not tenant_proved_unavoidable_inability

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant for non-payment of rent.
predicates.landlord_gave_two_month_arrears_notice: The landlord gave the tenant two months' notice demanding payment of rent arrears.
predicates.rent_arrears_remained_after_notice: The tenant did not clear all rent arrears after receiving the notice.
predicates.tenant_proved_unavoidable_inability: The tenant proved that unavoidable circumstances made the tenant incapable of paying the rent.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding for non-payment, when rent arrears remain unpaid after the landlord's two-month demand notice and the tenant has not proved unavoidable inability to pay, the tenant has committed wilful rent default.
